name: APT29 - SolarWinds Compromise (C0024)
description: Techniques MITRE ATT&CK documents for the SolarWinds Compromise (C0024), attributed to APT29 (G0016).

techniques.comment: APT29 gained access to victims through a trojanized SolarWinds Orion software update. SUNSPOT was used to insert SUNBURST into the Orion build process.
SUNBURST was incorporated into the Orion software lifecycle and signed using legitimate SolarWinds code-signing certificates.
APT29 used PowerShell to execute commands, create remote tasks, identify configurations, and conduct other post-compromise activities.
APT29 used Get-ADUser and Get-ADGroupMember to identify domain accounts.
The group used Get-AcceptedDomain and AdFind to identify domains and trust relationships.
APT29 stole saved Chrome passwords from targeted users.
The attackers added credentials to OAuth applications and service principals.
APT29 granted administrator privileges to a newly created service principal.
APT29 modified federation trust settings so the victim environment would accept tokens signed with the attackers' SAML certificate.
The attackers created forged SAML tokens using compromised SAML signing certificates to impersonate legitimate users.
APT29 used compromised service principals and associated authentication material to access and modify Office 365 environments.
APT29 used RDP sessions from public-facing systems to internal servers.
The attackers used administrative accounts to connect to targeted users through SMB.
APT29 used WinRM through PowerShell to execute commands and payloads on remote hosts.
APT29 created or modified scheduled tasks to execute tools remotely and maintain persistence.
The group used Exchange mailbox commands to collect emails from selected executives and IT personnel.
APT29 downloaded source code from victim code repositories.
Collected files and data were staged in password-protected archives on an OWA server.
APT29 used 7-Zip to compress stolen email and other information into password-protected archives.
HTTP was used for command and control and data exfiltration.
APT29 used dynamic DNS resolution to construct and resolve randomly generated subdomains for C2.
Collected information was exfiltrated using HTTPS requests to password-protected archives staged on OWA servers.
APT29 used AUDITPOL to prevent the collection of audit logs.
The attackers used netsh to modify firewall rules and restrict certain outbound traffic.
